title: Inverse semialgebras and partial actions of Lie algebras: the Lie inverse semialgebra E(L) governs the premorphisms defined on L (Theorem 4.10)
author: Mikhailo Dokuchaev, Farangis Johari, and Jose L. Vilca-Rodriguez
work: Inverse semialgebras and partial actions of Lie algebras
difficulty_reason: The counted theorem is one of the article's main results: it is the Lie-theoretic analogue of Exel's correspondence between premorphisms of a group into an inverse monoid and homomorphisms of the Exel semigroup, and it is not a qualification exercise. With the whole preliminary apparatus available as context - the inverse semivector spaces, the Lie inverse semialgebras, the pivotal Proposition 2.20 that E(L) is a Lie inverse semialgebra, Lemma 4.3 that the canonical map tau is a strong premorphism, Lemma 4.8 on the infimum of idempotents and Corollary 4.9 on its additivity - the author still has to run a source-local argument: define the extension of a premorphism by the infimum formula, verify well-definedness through Lemma 4.8, recover the identity on L, prove additivity of the extension by combining the premorphism identity with the additivity of the infimum of idempotents, prove homogeneity in the scalar and invoke the linearity criterion of Remark 2.4, then establish the bracket identity by expanding the bracket of two values of the extension, using the compatibility inequality to compare the mixed brackets with the zero-idempotent brackets and reducing the expression to the extension of the bracket, and finally prove uniqueness by a generator-by-generator computation on the idempotent part. Every step is carried out inside the new structure rather than quoted, so the unit sits above ordinary PhD qualifying examinations in algebra.
